title: Console UX for data residency: settings, confirmations, and blocked-request troubleshooting
creator: Naomi Feldman
project: Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation: Hosted data residency enforcement
description:
Goal
Design Console UX for configuring Hosted data residency region pinning and for troubleshooting residency enforcement blocks. Deliver: (1) Residency settings page(s), (2) confirmation / warning modals for risky changes, (3) “Blocked requests” troubleshooting view with copy guidelines aligned to the public error contract.

Context
Enterprise customers (EU regulated, healthcare/payments) need to pin Hosted API processing to specific regions (e.g., EU-only) and understand why requests are blocked when configuration is misaligned. The Console must make policy intent clear, prevent foot-guns, and provide actionable troubleshooting without exposing sensitive content.

Primary UX surfaces (scope)
1) Residency settings
- Location: Console → Organization Settings → Security & Compliance → Data residency
- Primary actions:
  a) View current residency policy state (inheritance + effective policy)
  b) Set/modify allowed regions + primary region
  c) Optional: API key–level overrides (if enabled for org) or per-project overrides (depending on policy model)
  d) View configuration history (audit events) and who changed what

2) Confirmation modals
- Confirm enabling enforcement and/or narrowing allowed regions.
- Confirm changes that may block traffic (e.g., switching EU-only to EU+US is less risky; switching EU+US → EU-only is risky).
- Provide remediation guidance: update SDK base URL/region, rotate keys, update routing hints, validate region mapping.

3) Troubleshooting: Blocked requests
- Location: Console → Observability → Requests → “Blocked (Residency)” (or a tab within Data residency)
- Show recent enforcement blocks with enough detail to fix configuration quickly.
- Must NOT display customer content (prompts/responses). Only metadata required for debugging.

Key user stories
- As an org admin, I can pin Hosted API processing to EU-only and set a primary region (e.g., eu-west) for predictable latency.
- As a platform admin, I can understand policy precedence (org vs project vs API key) and what policy is effective.
- As an on-call engineer / support, I can quickly answer: “Why are requests blocked?” and “What should the customer change?”

Information architecture + precedence (UI expectations)
We need to visualize effective policy and inheritance. Proposed pattern:
- “Effective policy” card at top with:
  - Status: Enabled/Disabled
  - Allowed regions: list
  - Primary region: single value
  - Policy source: Organization / Project / API key (and link)
  - Last updated: timestamp + actor
- Below, configuration sections:
  - Organization policy (editable)
  - Project overrides (if supported; link to per-project list)
  - API key overrides (if supported; link to keys list)

If policy model is finalized as Org + optional Project + optional API key:
- Show a small precedence helper: “Most specific wins: API key → Project → Organization.”
- Provide an “Effective policy simulator” interaction: choose Project + API key (dropdowns) and display the effective policy.

Residency settings: detailed requirements
A) Region selection control
- Control: multi-select for Allowed regions; single-select for Primary region.
- Constraint: Primary region must be a member of Allowed regions.
- UX rule: Disallow saving if Allowed regions is empty or Primary region is not selected.
- Add helper text: “Requests will only be processed in allowed regions. Redwood will not route or fall back outside these regions unless explicitly permitted.”

B) Enforcement toggle
- Toggle: “Enforce data residency (Hosted API)”
- When OFF: show “Not enforced” state; warnings that routing may use other regions for reliability.
- When ON: explain expected behavior at request time (blocking vs fallback).
- Copy must align with policy narrative: deterministic checks; no cross-region fallback unless allowed.

C) Validation + inline errors
- Inline validation messages under fields (avoid toast-only errors).
- Validation cases:
  - No allowed regions selected
  - Primary region not selected
  - Primary region not in allowed set
  - Attempted policy conflicts with existing Dedicated/Private settings (if relevant; likely informational only)
- For server-side validation failure: show error banner with request ID.

D) Save flow
- “Review changes” step when risk is high (see modals below).
- Save button label: “Save residency policy”
- Show loading state and a success confirmation with link to “View recent blocks” for verification.

Confirmation modal designs (copy + logic)
Triggering conditions
1) Enabling enforcement
- Trigger: toggle OFF → ON
- Message intent: warn about possible blocks; provide verification steps.

2) Narrowing allowed regions
- Trigger: removing any previously-allowed region OR changing primary region
- Message intent: this may block requests routed/targeted to a disallowed region.

3) Changing precedence-impacting overrides
- Trigger: enabling API key overrides feature for org OR adding an API key override that is more restrictive than org policy.

Modal content requirements
- Title: clear, non-alarming but explicit.
- Body:
  - “What will happen” bullets
  - “What to check before saving” bullets
  - “How to roll back” / “How to temporarily mitigate” (if we support a feature flag/override; otherwise omit)
- Primary CTA: “Save and enforce” / “Save changes”
- Secondary CTA: “Cancel”

Draft copy (v1)
Modal 1: Enable enforcement
- Title: “Turn on data residency enforcement?”
- Body:
  - “After you enable enforcement, requests that would be processed outside your allowed regions will be blocked.”
  - “Before enabling: verify your clients are targeting your primary region and that any routing hints match your allowed regions.”
  - “You can troubleshoot blocked requests in Console → Data residency → Blocked requests.”
- Primary CTA: “Enable enforcement”

Modal 2: Narrow allowed regions
- Title: “This change may block requests”
- Body:
  - “You removed one or more allowed regions. Requests that target or fall back to those regions will be blocked.”
  - “Recommended: update client configuration to use the primary region, then monitor blocked requests after saving.”
- Primary CTA: “Save changes”

Modal 3: Change primary region
- Title: “Change primary region?”
- Body:
  - “New requests will prefer the new primary region. If your clients explicitly target a different region, they may be blocked depending on your allowed regions.”
- Primary CTA: “Change primary region”

Troubleshooting: “Blocked requests” view
Goals
- Reduce support load by letting admins self-diagnose common causes (wrong base URL/region; using an API key with different policy; stale SDK config; project override).
- Provide request correlation fields without revealing prompt/response.

Proposed UI components
A) Summary banner (top)
- “Blocked requests in last 1h / 24h” count
- Link: “View docs: Data residency troubleshooting” (docs PR will add help URL)

B) Table (default: last 24h)
Columns:
- Timestamp
- Request ID (click to details; copy button)
- Endpoint (e.g., /v1/chat/completions)
- Attempted region (the region the request would have been processed in OR the client-requested region, depending on enforcement context)
- Allowed regions (effective)
- Policy source (Org / Project / API key) + link to the policy config
- Error code (machine-readable)

C) Filters
- Time range (1h, 24h, 7d)
- Project
- API key (admin-only, redacted display)
- Attempted region
- Error code

D) Request details drawer
- Request ID (copy)
- Error code + message (exactly as returned by gateway; see copy guidelines)
- Effective policy ID (if we expose policy_id) and policy source
- Evaluated allowed regions + primary region
- “Why it was blocked” (short explanation)
- “How to fix” actions:
  - “Review residency settings” deep link
  - “Update client region/base URL” (docs link)
  - “Check API key policy” (deep link)
- Note: do not show prompt, response, or payload.

E) Empty + loading states
- Empty: “No residency blocks in the selected time range.” plus “Verify enforcement is enabled and that clients are using the primary region.”

Copy + terminology guidelines (align with Product + ADR)
Terminology
- Use: “Data residency”, “Allowed regions”, “Primary region”, “Enforcement”, “Blocked request”, “Residency policy”.
- Avoid: “Geo-fencing”, “sovereignty lock”, “hard pin” (unless legal asks).
- Always specify: “Hosted API” when relevant (avoid confusion with Dedicated/Private).

Error content in UI
- Must mirror gateway error contract (ADR-022 / PM-1490):
  - Show HTTP status (if available in UI)
  - Show error_code exactly
  - Show request_id
  - If included: policy_id (confirm whether exposed externally; if not, keep internal-only)
  - Include a “Learn more” help_url
- Avoid rewriting the error message in a way that conflicts with SDK surfaced messages. Prefer: show the same text and add additional “How to fix” section.

Accessibility + i18n constraints
- All modal titles and button labels must be concise and screen-reader friendly.
- Avoid constructing long sentences from concatenated variables; use short sentences with labeled fields.

Deliverables
- Wireframes (settings page, modals, blocked table, details drawer)
- Final UI copy doc (strings list + usage notes)
- Engineering handoff notes (fields required from APIs; redaction guidance)

Open questions
1) Policy identifiers: Are we showing policy_id in Console? (PM thread suggests maybe yes for admins; verify with PM-1490 / ADR-022.)
2) What’s the canonical list of region display names vs internal IDs? Need mapping from infra sheet for UI labels.
3) Where should “Blocked requests” live: under Data residency settings vs Observability → Requests? Proposed: link from settings, but primary surface under Data residency for discoverability.
4) Do we support per-project policies in v1 GA or only org-level? UI should gracefully degrade (hide sections) based on feature flags.

Acceptance criteria
- Console shows “Effective policy” including allowed regions + primary region + policy source.
- Org admin can enable enforcement and set allowed regions/primary region with clear inline validation.
- Risky changes show confirmation modal(s) with agreed copy.
- “Blocked requests” view shows last 24h blocks with filters and a details drawer; includes request_id and error_code; no customer content displayed.
- Copy aligns with PM-1490 and ADR-022 (error code names, help link structure, and tone).

Notes for engineering handoff (data needed)
- Effective policy endpoint should provide: allowed_regions[], primary_region, enforcement_enabled, policy_source, updated_at, updated_by.
- Blocked request event feed should provide: timestamp, request_id, endpoint, attempted_region, effective_allowed_regions, effective_primary_region, policy_source, error_code, message, help_url (optional), project_id, api_key_id (admin-only; should be partially redacted in UI).

Related work
- PM-1490 (error messaging contract)
- ENG-4833 (gateway standardized errors, streaming parity)
- ENG-4846 (metrics for blocked requests; can power Console counts)

Progress updates

- 2025-02-14 (Naomi): Confirmed terminology: “Allowed regions” + “Primary region” + “Enforcement”. Avoid “geo-fencing”.
- 2025-02-19 (Felix): Updated modal copy to match PM-1490 language; added request details drawer fields to avoid payload display.
